result_text:
`all_files.zip` is now built from the configured aspect names, so renaming `buildAndDeployment` no longer breaks the export.

The change is in `reports/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/reports/dataexporters/DataExporter.java`, in the `try` block at the end of `exportJson()`. The five hardcoded `aspect_*.txt` entries are replaced by a loop over the five scope aspects. For each aspect it calls `DataExportUtils.getAspectFileListFileName(aspect, "")`, the same call the loose files are written with. The entries keep the same order. With the default config the names are unchanged. With `buildAndDeployment` renamed, the fourth entry becomes `aspect_buildAndDeployment.txt`.

The old code threw `FileNotFoundException` on the missing file, and the catch-all then skipped `git-history.zip` too. With the lookup fixed, that exception no longer happens, so `git-history.zip` is written again whenever `git-history.txt` exists.

The reports module compiles and its offline tests pass (`mvn -q -o -pl reports test`). I did not run an export with a renamed aspect end to end.

`codeanalyzer/.../landscape/analysis/LandscapeAnalyzer.java` (around lines 280–283) has the same hardcoded `aspect_build_and_deployment.txt` literal. I left it alone because it is outside this export fix, but a renamed aspect would break the landscape repository file lookup the same way.

Nothing is committed.
